name: Perspectives and Missing Voices
title: Perspectives and Missing Voices
answer: Perspectives and Missing Voices is a social studies use of AI in which a tool helps students compare how different people might describe the same event and helps teachers find groups that textbooks often leave out. It matters because it can build empathy and critical thinking while pointing toward missing parts of the curriculum. The AI output is only a starting point, and every suggested lead or simulated viewpoint must be checked against real sources before it is taught.

crumbs.name: Social Studies, Civics, and World Languages

sections.body: This idea addresses two related gaps in social studies. First, students can struggle to see an event from more than one point of view, so AI can generate contrasting perspectives for them to compare and discuss. Second, teachers may not know which groups were involved in a historical event but rarely appear in textbooks, so AI can suggest leads for further investigation. The purpose is not to replace the historical record but to spark inquiry and help students ask better questions. By comparing differing views and then searching for real sources, students practice both empathy and critical thinking.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a teacher might ask an AI tool how a factory owner, a factory worker, and a child laborer would each describe working conditions in 1900. Students then compare those views, discuss why they differ, and look for real sources that support or challenge each one. A teacher might also ask which groups were involved in a historical event but rarely appear in textbooks, using the suggestions as leads to follow rather than facts to teach. The text does not give grade bands for these activities, so the approach is described generally. Perspective activities work best when they end with real sources, so students move from a simulated viewpoint to real letters, diaries, and records.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The supplied text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It presents the approach as a practical teaching use of AI rather than as a research-backed intervention. This idea therefore rests on practice rather than research. The text's claims about building empathy and critical thinking are stated as purposes and benefits, not as measured outcomes.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text sets clear limits. AI suggestions are leads to follow, not facts to teach, and every lead must be checked in library databases or trusted collections because chatbots can invent sources that sound convincing. A simulated perspective is a starting point for inquiry, not a substitute for the historical record. The teacher keeps the decisions about which leads to pursue, which real sources to use, and how to guide discussion. Students should move from the simulation to real letters, diaries, and records, with the sources answering the question the simulation sparked.
